body.statement: There is a finite constant \(C_{\beta}\), depending only on \(\beta\), such that uniformly over \(m\ge2\), \(P\in\mathcal H_{\beta,D}(m)\), and \(\pi\in\Pi_m\), \(\lvert\log V_{P,\tau}(\pi)-\bar t_P^{\pi}\rvert\le C_{\beta}D\tau^{\beta/4}\). The conclusion holds for right-continuous survivals with atoms and for arbitrarily small \(\tau\).
body.justification: This gives a nonsingular deterministic bridge from heterogeneous survival mixtures to log-sum-exp cores without a density lower bound.
body.gap: CarpentierKim2015 controls a single second-order Pareto tail coefficient, while EinmahlHe2023 studies predetermined average tails; neither supplies policy-uniform generalized-quantile inversion over changing heterogeneous mixtures.
body.consumer: Every regret and confidence-width calculation can be carried out on the smooth Pareto core and transferred back to the original atom-permitting class.
